Quick & Easy

Lemon, Pea & Ricotta Pasta

Short pasta tossed in a light ricotta and lemon sauce, with sweet green peas cooked in the same pot. The starchy pasta water brings everything together into a creamy, bright bowl without heavy cream.

Prep
~20 min
Method
Stovetop
Total
~20 min
Ingredients & Method ↓

Development edition · Awaits kitchen testing.

Ingredients Method Storage

Ingredients

How many people?
2

Estimated to serve 2 people as a main meal.

  • 180 g dry short pasta
  • 150 g frozen peas
  • 120 g ricotta cheese
    Missing this?

    Use mashed or whipped cottage cheese · 120 g

    Similar creaminess, but may have small curds unless blended. Cottage cheese can be saltier, so taste before adding extra salt. Adjust the pasta water gradually, as moisture levels vary. Mash or blend before mixing for a smoother sauce.

  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice, plus more to taste
  • ½ tsp lemon zest
  • Salt and black pepper to taste
  • reserved pasta water, as needed

Contains wheat (pasta) and dairy (ricotta). Check all ingredient labels.

Method

You'll need
Large pot · Large mixing bowl

01

Cook the pasta and peas

Cook the pasta according to package directions. Add the frozen peas near the end, respecting their required cooking time. Reserve a cup of the pasta water before draining.

Look for: Pasta is cooked to the package's suggested doneness.

02

Prepare the ricotta base

In a large bowl, mash the ricotta with the olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, and black pepper. Add a few spoonfuls of the hot reserved pasta water to loosen the mixture.

Look for: The mixture should look creamy and slightly thinned out.

03

Combine and adjust

Add the drained pasta and peas to the bowl. Toss well, adding more pasta water gradually until the sauce coats the pasta. Adjust salt to taste and serve.

Look for: The sauce adheres to the pasta without looking dry or forming a puddle at the bottom.

Serve with

Serve immediately while warm and creamy.

One way to change it up

Storage & Prep ahead

This dish is best eaten fresh. The ricotta sauce will absorb into the pasta if left sitting.

Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water to loosen the sauce.
